test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: Which of the following articles guarantees the Right to Equality before the Law and the Right to Equal Protection of the Laws?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 14**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 14** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Equality before the Law and the Right to Equal Protection of the Laws.
 
• This article is a fundamental right that ensures all individuals are treated equally by the law.
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• Article 14 applies to both citizens and non-citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• Article 14 is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The right to equality is a cornerstone of the Indian legal system and is crucial for maintaining the rule of law in the country.
